messages:
samw: Heads-up — sketching a proposal for per-plan routing slices + graceful throttle/fallbacks. want feedback on API shape and enforcement model.

anya: +1. quick Q: do we treat free/pro/enterprise as orthogonal to region? e.g., EU-enterprise gets different variant than US-enterprise?

samw: yes, plan + region both matter. priority order: (1) tenant overrides, (2) plan-region slice, (3) plan default, (4) global default.

leo: sounds reasonable. what about quota enforcement? hard quota for free, soft quota with throttles for pro, guaranteed throughput for enterprise?

rachel: prefer soft-first for pro: soft window=60s, grace tokens, then fallback to lower-cost variant rather than hard 429s. enterprise gets backpressure+alerts.

samw: example policy YAML:

```yaml
slices:
  - name: enterprise-eu
    plan: enterprise
    region: eu
    allowed_models: [rubin-2q, rubin-2q-int8]
    max_rps: 500
    fallback_order: [rubin-2q-int8, rubin-1.5]
    enforcement: guaranteed
  - name: pro-global
    plan: pro
    region: global
    max_rps: 200
    enforcement: soft
    soft_window: 60
    fallback_order: [rubin-2q-int8, rubin-1.5]
  - name: free-global
    plan: free
    region: global
    max_rps: 10
    enforcement: hard
    fallback_order: [rubin-1.5]
```

anya: couple notes: need to add fair-share weighting when multiple tenants hit the same slice, and telemetry tags: plan, slice_name, fallback_used, enforcement_step.

samw: agreed. telemetry we should emit these metrics: token_cost, latency_p50/p95, fallback_count by variant, throttle_count, dropped_requests.

deploy-bot: deploy requested by samw at 2026-03-20T14:12:03Z — job queued :gear:

leo: for console UX, propose a visual timeline per-slice showing usage vs max_rps and overlay fallback events. also editable fallback_order via drag/drop.

rachel: rollout plan: start with pro-global soft enforcement for 2 weeks, watch fallback_count and latency regressions, then expand. If fallback_count > 5% for 24h, rollback.

anya: API schema debate: should we expose enforcement enum {hard,soft,guaranteed} or break into fields (soft_window, guaranteed_min_rps)? I prefer explicit fields for clarity.

samw: leaning explicit fields. fewer surprise semantics. we'll add server-side validation and a safe default: enforcement=soft if unspecified.

leo: minor: ensure rate-limiter supports token-bucket with per-slice burst and tenant min-guarantees.

rachel: ok i'll write the rollout doc + dashboard mockups. Sam — can you open a PR with the policy proto and example YAML?

samw: will do today. thanks all :thumbsup:
